contexts.text: Thou shalt not take the name of thy God into what is vain = ... that each and all things which belong to the worship of God are not to be contemned, still less blasphemed and contaminated with filthy things. AC 8882. TCR 297, Explained.
Good... could not manifest itself, because... vain and empty things were outside of it, such as the things which are of the glory of the world and of self.
(Divine truths appearing as) vain. Signified, Explained.

To take into what is vain = to profane and blaspheme. By to take the name of God into what is vain, is properly signified to turn truth into evil, that is, to believe that it is truth, and still to live in evil; and it is also to turn good into falsity, that is, to live holily and yet not to believe: both are profanation. Explained.
See Name. TCR 297. TCR 298. TCR 299.
Thou shalt not take up a report of vanity () = no listening to Falsities... Vanity = Falsity... of doctrine and religion. Illustrated.
Vanity () = Falsity of doctrine; a lie = falsity of life.
They said, We know that it is an imaginary nothingness. Described.
The wives murmured. What woman is so devoid of vanity as not to want to seem beautiful to men (in general).
It is vain to want to Know...
(This) is a vanity of vanities.

Everyone can be regenerated according to his state... in one way those who from infancy have entered into the vanities of the world, and in another way those who earlier or later have withdrawn from them.
The imputation of this faith is vain.
To name the Lord from proprium is to take His name into what is vain.
This (falsification of the truths of the Word) is... meant by the vanities which the prophets see, and the lies which they speak. AE 624:13.
Vanities = such things as are of no account; and lies = falsities.

He that offereth frankincense, blesseth vanity () = to worship God from such things as represented spiritual good, and yet to love evil and falsity and imbue them... Vanity = evil, and the falsity of evil.
The falsities from which is such worship, are signified by they have burnt incense to vanity (): vanity = falsity.
Vanities () = falsities.
Vanities of strangers () = falsities of religion.
Egypt, a vanity and emptiness () = the Sensuous and the Natural, which, regarded in themselves, are devoid of good and also of truths.
All the rest are in vain.
